Bid choosers with many bids

Your Bridge pick taken to the games with many bids: one chooser over one row of buttons, both the same width, the white card on the picked bid, no lines, square cells and the lowest bid you can make picked at the start. Spades and Twenty-Nine have fourteen bids, Double Deck Pinochle 49 and Pinochle 76. Each version is a way to hold that many. Tap the bids to try them. Every piece is drawn by the site’s own stylesheet.

What changes for the player

Today a tap on a bid sends it at once. With a chooser the lowest bid you can make is picked at the start, so the usual bid, one over the last, is still one tap: the button. Any other bid is two taps, the bid and then the button, and the button shows the bid before it goes.

Spades has no Pass, so its row is your bid alone. Its lowest bid is Nil, which carries its own rules, so a Spades chooser starts on 1.

Two rows of seven show fourteen bids, so Spades and Twenty-Nine need no arrows. Pinochle needs six pages and Double Deck four. Each page starts at the lowest bid you can make, so a bid you cannot make is only shown near the top.

Questions for you

  • Which version? Two rows of seven, one row of seven, the stepper or the slider? It can differ by game.
  • Where do the arrows go? Here they sit in the row of buttons, where today’s Pinochle box has them. They could also be cells at the ends of the chooser.
  • What should be picked at the start? The lowest bid you can make, or the hint’s bid, the one the game’s own bot would make?

How it would be built

For the redesign only. The chooser is the suit pill’s paper with number cells (the Bridge lab’s text cell), one mark and, for two rows, a mark that moves between them. The stepper and the slider are the same pill with an arrow cell at each end, drawn as the pill draws a suit. The pager in the row of buttons is today’s back and forth button on the felt. The proposal rules are at the bottom of chooser-lab-parts/lab.css. In the code it touches each game’s showBid and the bid spots in its layout.
